title: HablaBA: From Local Research to a Working Product
description: Turns Buenos Aires language-exchange research into an invite-only web product for finding small local sessions and coordinating them in real time.
seoTitle: HablaBA Project | Local Language Exchange MVP
seoDescription: How I built HablaBA, an invite-only Buenos Aires language-exchange product with local sessions, real-time chat, notifications, and trust controls.
timeline: Research, prototyping, and product build from June to October 2025
deliveryHighlights: Product direction shaped by a group interview, an 11-response survey, and six usability sessions
Invite-only onboarding, verified email, guided profiles, and admin-controlled invitation links
One-to-one and small-group exchange sessions organized by language, neighborhood, time, and open seats
Private real-time chat with in-app and browser notifications for each exchange
outcomes: Moved from research and an interactive prototype to a full-stack product with the core exchange loop implemented
Used usability findings to choose an exchange-first model, real profile photos, and focused coordination over a profile feed
constraints: The product had to support trust between people planning in-person meetings without becoming another dating-style profile browser.
Small exchanges needed enough structure to set expectations while staying lightweight to create and join.
Chat and notifications had to help people coordinate a session without becoming a separate social feed.
The architecture changed during the build, so the final product needed to preserve the core workflow while consolidating the web stack.
problem: Language learners in Buenos Aires had plenty of places to browse profiles or attend large events, but those options often made focused practice harder to arrange.

A three-person group interview, an 11-response survey, and six usability sessions pointed toward a smaller, local experience organized around a specific exchange rather than an open-ended social network.
solution: Designed HablaBA around one-to-one and small-group exchange sessions with clear languages, neighborhoods, times, participant limits, and a private chat for coordination.

Added invite-only registration, email verification, guided profile setup, two-factor authentication, and admin-controlled invitation links so access and trust were part of the product rather than launch notes.
Connected exchange updates, real-time messages, in-app notifications, and browser push notifications so a plan could move from discovery to a session.

Built separate React Native/Expo and Flutter clients against the earlier Rails API, then consolidated the maintained web product into Laravel 12, Inertia, and Vue with PostgreSQL, Redis, Reverb, queues, and a containerized production setup.
result: HablaBA became a working web product that covers invitation, profile setup, discovery, session creation and joining, private chat, and notifications.
The build turned the research into concrete product decisions, including an exchange-first information model, small participant limits, neighborhood filters, and real photos for in-person trust.
